findings.title: Cache never invalidated, returns stale data
findings.description: monthly_summary now returns whatever was cached for (user_id, month) forever. If an expense is added, edited, or deleted for that month after the first call, the cached totals are stale and the dashboard will show incorrect numbers for the rest of the process lifetime. There is no invalidation hook in add_expense/set_budget or anywhere else, so this is a real correctness regression, not just a performance optimization.

findings.title: Cache key omits db instance
findings.description: The cache key is (user_id, month) only, not including the db connection/instance. Any two different database instances (e.g. separate test fixtures, separate SQLite files, or a prod db vs a per-request db handle) sharing the same user_id and month will incorrectly return each other's cached results. Since _summary_cache is a module-level global, this also leaks state across test runs sharing a user id/month, causing test order-dependent flakiness and, in a multi-tenant deployment scenario with multiple db handles, could serve one database's data as if it belonged to another.

findings.title: Unbounded module-level cache growth
findings.description: _summary_cache is a plain dict with no eviction policy, TTL, or size bound. In a long-running dashboard process it will accumulate an entry per distinct (user_id, month) forever, growing without limit as new users/months are queried, which is a memory leak in a long-lived service.

findings.title: Test does not cover cache invalidation or key correctness
findings.description: The added test only calls monthly_summary twice back-to-back with no state change in between, so it trivially passes even though the underlying implementation never invalidates on data changes and keys only on (user_id, month) without the db. A meaningful test should add an expense, call monthly_summary to populate the cache, add another expense, call monthly_summary again, and assert the totals reflect the new expense (which would currently fail), plus verify isolation across different db instances with the same user_id/month.
